chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Verily God is more exalted and more noble than to be known through His creatures; rather, the creatures are known through God.' He said: 'You have spoken the truth.' I said: 'Whoever recognizes that he has a Lord, it is befitting for him to recognize that for that Lord there is pleasure and wrath, and that His pleasure and His wrath cannot be known except through revelation or a messenger.

So whoever does not receive revelation, it is befitting for him to seek the messengers, and when he meets them he recognizes that they are the Divine Authority and that obedience to them is obligatory.' And I said to the people: 'Do you know that the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) was the Divine Authority from God over His creatures?' They said: 'Yes.' I said: 'So when the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) passed away, who was the Divine Authority over His creatures?' So they said: 'The Quran.'

So I looked into the Quran and found that the Murji'ite, and the Qadariyya, and the atheist who does not believe in it all dispute using it, to the point of overpowering men through argumentation. So I recognized that the Quran cannot serve as a Divine Authority except with a custodian, and whatever he says concerning it would be true. So I said to them: 'Who is the custodian of the Quran?' They said: 'Ibn Mas'ud had some knowledge, and Umar had some knowledge, and Hudhayfa had some knowledge.' I said: 'All of it?' They said: 'No.'

So I found no one who could be said to know all of it except Ali (peace be upon him). And when a matter arose among the people, this one said 'I don't know', and this one said 'I don't know', and this one said 'I don't know', but this one said 'I do know.' So I testify that Ali (peace be upon him) was the custodian of the Quran, and obedience to him was obligatory, and he was the Divine Authority over the people after the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family),
and that whatever he said regarding the Quran is the truth.' So he (the Imam) said: 'May God have mercy on you.'

key_terms.الزِّنْدِيق: Atheist/Zindiq — in early Islamic usage, a materialist or crypto-dualist who denies revelation
key_terms.الطَّاعَة الْمُفْتَرَضَة: Obligatory obedience — obedience that is divinely mandated
key_terms.الْحُجَّة: Divine Authority/Proof (hujja) — the authoritative representative of God on earth, who constitutes a binding proof upon humankind
key_terms.الْقَدَرِيّ: Qadariyya — early theological group who affirmed absolute human free will
key_terms.الْمُرْجِئ: Murji'ite — member of an early Islamic theological school who deferred judgment on sinners
key_terms.قَيِّم: Custodian/guardian — one who stands over, maintains, and authoritatively interprets the Quran

ai.seo_question: Why did Mansur ibn Hazim argue that the Quran alone is insufficient as a Divine Authority without an Imam?
ai.summary: Mansur ibn Hazim, a trusted companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), recounts to the Imam a rational argument he used to establish the necessity of a living Divine Authority (hujja) after the Prophet. He begins from the premise that God's pleasure and wrath can only be known through revelation or a messenger, then demonstrates that the Quran alone cannot serve as an authority without a qualified interpreter. Through dialogue with his contemporaries, he eliminates all candidates until only Imam Ali (AS) remains as the one who possesses complete knowledge of the Quran. The Imam endorses his reasoning with the supplication 'May God have mercy on you' — a characteristic expression of deep approval in early Shia discourse.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is more Majestic and more Benevolent than that He<sup>azwj</sup> should be recognised by His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures. But, the creatures are being recognised by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You speak the truth’.

I said, ‘The one who recognises that there is a Lord<sup>azwj</sup> for him, so it is befitting for him that he recognises that for that Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, there is Pleasure and Anger, and that he (himself) would not recognise His<sup>azwj</sup> Pleasure and His<sup>azwj</sup> Anger except by a Revelation or by a Rasool<sup>saww</sup>. So the one to whom the Revelation does not come, so it would be befitting for him that he seeks the Rasools<sup>as</sup>, and when he meets up with them<sup>as</sup>, he should recognise that he<sup>as</sup> is the Divine Authority and that there is an obedience to them<sup>as</sup>, the Necessitated obedience.
And I said to the people, ‘Do you know that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was the Divine Authority from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures?’ They said, ‘Yes’. I said, ‘So when Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> passed away, who was the Divine Authority upon His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures?’ So they said, ‘The Quran’.

So I looked into the Quran, so it was such what the Murjiites, and the Qadiriyya were debating with, and (even) the atheists who do not believe in it, to the extent that they overcome the men by debating with it. So I recognised that the Quran cannot happen to be a Divine Authority except by a custodian, so he<sup>asws</sup> would not say anything with regards to it except that it would be true.

So I said to them, ‘Who is the custodian of the Quran?’ So they said, ‘Ibn Masoud. He had known, and Umar knew, and Huzayfa knew’. I said, ‘(They knew) all of it?’ They said, ‘No’. So I did not find anyone who could say that he knew all of that except for Ali<sup>asws</sup>. And whenever there was something between the people, so this one said, ‘I don’t know’, and this one said, ‘I don’t know’, and this one said, ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do know’. So I testify that Ali<sup>asws</sup> was the custodian of the Quran, and that obedience to him<sup>asws</sup> was a necessity, and he<sup>asws</sup> was the Divine Authority upon the people after Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and that whatever he<sup>asws</sup> said regarding the Quran, so it is true’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on you’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said the following.

“I said to Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.), ‘Allah by far above Majestic and Gracious to be known through His creatures. In fact, the creatures are known through Allah.’” The Imam (a.s.) said, “You have spoken the truth.” I said, “One who knows that he has a Lord, he must also learn that his Lord agrees with certain things and disagrees with certain other things. The only way he would know what his like and dislikes is revelation or a messenger.

On e does not receive revelation he must find the messengers and when finds the messengers he will know that they the Divine authority and that obedience to them is necessary. I say to people, “Do you know that the messenger of Allah was the Divine authority over His creatures?” They say, “Yes, he was the Divine authority.” I then ask, “After the messenger of Allah who was the Divine authority over His creatures?” They said, “After the messenger of Allah the Divine authority is the Holy Quran.”

I considered the Holy Quran and found out that various kinds of people consider this Holy Book as support for their beliefs. For example the Murji’a (people who say Allah has postponed punishment), the pre-determinists and the atheist who even do not believe in it but take it as the basis for their arguments against the others. I then learned that the Holy Quran can not serve as Divine authority without a guardian whose words from the Holy Quran would be the truth. I then ask the people, “Who is the guardian of the Holy Quran?” They say, “Ibn Mas‘ud knew the Holy Quran, ‘Umar knew it and Hudhayfa knew the Holy Quran.” I ask them, “Did they know all of the Holy Quran?” The people say, “No, they did not know all of it.”

I have not found anyone who would know all of the Holy Quran except Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.). It is a fact that if any issue would emerge that needed a Quranic solution, except for Imam Ali (a.s.) every one of the others would, in many cases, say, “I do not know.” Only Imam Ali (a.s.) would say, “I know.” I then acknowledge that Imam Ali (a.s.) is the guardian of the Holy Quran and obedience to him is obligatory and he is the Divine authority over the people after the Holy Prophet (s.a.).
Whatever Imam Ali (a.s.) has said from the Holy Quran is the truth.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “May Allah grant you blessing.”
